overview: The TP4056 chip implements exactly the constant-current-then-constant-voltage charge profile a lithium cell needs, and this small breakout board wraps it with a USB input connector and status LEDs, turning 'safely charge a LiPo/Li-ion cell' into 'plug in a USB cable.' Many boards on the market add a second chip (commonly a DW01 plus a small MOSFET) providing basic over-discharge, overcharge, and short-circuit protection on the battery output — worth checking for specifically, since a bare TP4056-only board handles charging safely but does nothing to protect the battery during discharge.
simpleSummary: A small board that safely charges a lithium battery from a USB cable.

specifications.chargeCurrent: Adjustable via a resistor (many boards fixed around 1A)
specifications.chargeProfile: Constant current, then constant voltage at 4.2V — standard Li-ion/LiPo profile
specifications.protectionCircuit: Present on boards with the extra DW01+MOSFET chip; absent on bare TP4056-only boards

pinMap.name: IN+ (USB)
pinMap.function: 5V power input, typically via the onboard USB connector.

pinMap.name: B+
pinMap.function: Battery positive terminal — connects directly to the cell being charged.

pinMap.name: B-
pinMap.gotcha: On protected boards, B- runs through the protection MOSFET, not straight to ground — don't assume B- and OUT- are the same net on protected variants.

pinMap.name: OUT+
pinMap.function: Output to the load (present on protected boards) — passes battery power through the protection circuit.
pinMap.gotcha: Only present on protected boards — bare TP4056-only modules have no separate load output and no discharge protection at all.

useCases.title: USB-rechargeable project battery
useCases.scenario: Add USB charging to any LiPo/Li-ion-powered project without designing a custom charge circuit.

useCases.title: Safe battery-powered device with load protection
useCases.scenario: Use a protected-variant board's OUT+/OUT- to power a load while guarding against over-discharge.

oftenConfusedWith: Standalone BMS boards (protection-only, no charging capability)
oftenUpgradedTo: Multi-cell balance-charging modules for packs with more than one cell in series
